uncited: Splat Sorting and Composition is the object-order rendering step that transforms a set of transformed volumetric primitives into a final 2D image by resolving depth occlusion and blending transparency.

It solves the order-dependent transparency problem inherent in splatting, where incorrect draw order leads to visual artifacts, by sorting primitives along the view direction and accumulating their contributions via alpha blending.
Splatting compositing is performed along sheets (all pixels at once for a set of voxels), whereas ray-casting composites along rays (one sample at a time) [S10, unofficial].
Splat-every-sample produces darker images due to incorrect visibility determination.
When `cameraPositionProvider` is null, the `SplatNode` automatically sorts its splats for the scene camera's current position.
If `cameraPositionProvider` is provided, the node sorts splats for the viewpoint returned by that provider instead of the scene camera.
